data.title: IP Address
data.tagline: A network-layer address used to locate an interface and route data
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether an address points at localhost, the LAN, or the public internet.
data.description: In local development, 127.0.0.1 is the current device's loopback interface; a LAN address is reachable only within its routed network. Sharing localhost with a coworker still points to their own computer. A public IP alone does not mean anyone can connect: routing, ports, service listening, and access rules also matter.

learning.assumes: You have seen localhost or numeric addresses, or heard that others cannot reach your service.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether an address points at localhost, the LAN, or the public internet.

distinctions.label: Domain
distinctions.explanation: A domain is a human-friendly name resolved to an IP before access; an IP is a device's numeric address on the network.

distinctions.label: Port
distinctions.explanation: An IP locates which device; a port distinguishes services on the same device. Together they form a complete address.

explanation.title: 127.0.0.1: only this machine
explanation.text: localhost and 127.0.0.1 mean this very computer; anyone else using the address reaches their own machine.

explanation.title: LAN address: routed within a network
explanation.text: Private addresses such as 192.168.x.x and 10.x.x.x can be routed within their network; the service must also listen on a reachable interface, and firewall and network rules must allow the connection.

explanation.title: A public address: potentially reachable from the internet
explanation.text: A public address can be routed from the internet, but connections still depend on ports, service listening, firewalls, and other access rules; a domain name resolves to an address.

data.boundary: Listening address and access address are two things: if the service listens on localhost only, even giving a colleague the LAN address fails. When others cannot reach it, check the listening scope first, then the address type.

lessonPractice.title: Your project runs on localhost:3000 and a colleague wants to access your dev server. What address should you give?

options.label: localhost points only at their own computer; use a LAN address or deploy publicly
options.feedback: Correct. localhost is each machine's name for itself; a colleague needs a LAN or public address.

options.label: Just give localhost:3000; the same address should work
options.feedback: localhost on the colleague's machine points at themselves, not your service.

options.label: The port 3000 alone is enough
options.feedback: A port is only an entry on one device; without an IP or domain, no device can be located.

data.agentPrompt: The local service runs on localhost:3000 and my colleague cannot reach it. Tell me this machine's LAN address and confirm the dev server listens on all interfaces rather than localhost only; if public access is needed, explain where to deploy.
